title: Does widening the transferred JON-F to aBN1 circuit beyond the shortest paths remove the high-frequency over-response?
purpose: ADR-2026-009 withdrew the hypothesis that short-term depression explains why no single contact scale fits both the 100 Hz and 220 Hz reference points, on the ground that the reference is a whole-brain static simulation while the transferred circuit is a one-hop 41-neuron subgraph. This contract tests the structural alternative it left: that the over-response at high drive comes from the paths the shortest-path rule excluded.

supersedes.reason: The v1 H1 criterion was one-sided: 'the widened 220 Hz rate is below the one-hop 33.167 Hz'. The widened readout is silent at every candidate scale, so v1 scored H1 as passed on a readout that produced nothing. A criterion satisfied by silence cannot distinguish moderation toward the reference from total suppression, which is the vacuous-criterion defect this project has already had to repair elsewhere. The v1 artifact is retained and not edited; its H1 verdict must be read as superseded.
supersedes.v1_result_retained: GeNN parity passed at both path lengths, H2 failed at both, and the readout produced 0.0 Hz at all eleven scales and all three frequencies for K=2 and K=3.

circuit_selection.rule: keep every neuron v with forward_distance(inputs, v) + backward_distance(v, readouts) <= K, and every edge among the kept neurons

identity_control.requirement: at K = 1 the bounded-path rule must return exactly the circuit the shortest-path rule returns, by body-ID set and edge count
identity_control.why: the sweep's whole result is a comparison against the one-hop circuit, so the selection rule must be shown to reproduce it rather than assumed to

4.excluded: too large for the NumPy runner within the session; a GeNN-only follow-up

hypotheses.statement: At 0.15 mV per contact, the scale that best matched the 100 Hz reference in the one-hop circuit, the widened circuit's mean 220 Hz readout rate is moved toward the reference: strictly below the one-hop value of 33.167 Hz and strictly above zero.
hypotheses.test: 0.0 < mean over seeds of the 220 Hz bilateral readout rate at 0.15 mV per contact < 33.167 Hz

outcomes.moderated: 0 < rate < 33.167; the widened circuit moves the response toward the reference and H1 is supported
outcomes.suppressed: rate == 0; the widened circuit abolishes the response rather than moderating it, and H1 is NOT supported even though the one-sided v1 inequality holds
outcomes.not_moderated: rate >= 33.167; widening does not reduce the over-response

hypotheses.statement: Some single contact scale in the registered candidate grid reproduces both the 100 Hz and the 220 Hz reference means within one reference standard deviation. The one-hop circuit fails this.
hypotheses.test: exists scale s in the grid with |rate_100(s) - 0.933| <= 0.964 and |rate_220(s) - 4.633| <= 2.008

hypotheses.statement: Descriptive: the fraction of neurons in the widened circuit whose transmitter prediction makes them inhibitory under the zero unresolved-sign policy, and the fraction of edges they carry.
Mechanistic, descriptive: the signed contact composition of the drive arriving directly on each readout, and whether it is net excitatory or net inhibitory, at every path length including K = 1.
hypotheses.test: none; it is recorded so a silent or saturated readout can be attributed rather than guessed at

hypotheses.statement: Diagnostic, descriptive: whether the circuit as a whole is active at the parity condition, reported as total spikes and the number of distinct spiking neurons, and how many input bodies the bounded-path rule actually stimulates at each path length.
hypotheses.test: none; a silent readout inside an active circuit is a different finding from a dead circuit, and the two must be distinguishable in the artifact

protocol.gate_on_parity: the ND-04 sweep is blocked for a path length whose NumPy and GeNN runs disagree beyond the base tolerances
protocol.controls: the K = 1 selection identity control above, plus parity; this contract answers one structural question and is not a Stage 1 exit attempt

known_confound: The bounded-path rule does not only add interneurons: at K = 2 it admits 78 of the JON-F input bodies against the one-hop circuit's 39, because more inputs can reach a readout within two hops than within one. The stimulated drive therefore roughly doubles between K = 1 and K = 2. This strengthens a suppression finding, since more drive produces less output, and would weaken a moderation finding, since part of any reduction could not then be attributed to the added partners alone.
disclosure: The circuit sizes above were computed before the v1 contract was written; no rate had been simulated in any widened circuit when v1 was registered. The v1 sweep has since been executed, and its outcome is recorded under `supersedes` above, so H1's corrected criterion is not blind to the result it will be scored against. What is blind is nothing: this contract is a post-hoc correction of a criterion, and it must be read as such rather than as a preregistration.
claim_boundary: A structural sensitivity test of a transferred, bounded open-loop circuit against archived FlyWire simulation output. It cannot award V1, V2 or V3, and even a pass on H2 would be a fit of one scale to two simulation-derived points.
